subdomains.business_boundary: Design, operation, and optimization of energy generation, transmission, and distribution systems plus building energy and nuclear power systems, spanning power engineering, building simulation, and nuclear reactor engineering.
subdomains.occupations: Power systems engineer; Building energy/HVAC simulation engineer; Nuclear reactor/thermal-hydraulics engineer; Energy optimization and control engineer
subdomains.boundary_note: Official ALE examples are building-energy MPC and 10kV feeder reliability; boundary overlaps mechanical/HVAC on building simulation and civil/structural at nuclear containment.

subdomains.business_boundary: Discovery, extraction, and production of mineral and hydrocarbon resources, covering petroleum reservoir engineering, production/completions design, and mine planning and geomechanics.
subdomains.occupations: Petroleum reservoir engineer; Production/completions engineer; Mining planning engineer; Geomechanics/rock-mechanics engineer
subdomains.boundary_note: uncovered_official=true: zero active official ALE tasks, so all candidates are industry-sourced (E3) or project hypotheses (E4); overlaps energy_power on flow simulation and civil engineering on slope stability.

subdomains.business_boundary: Digital integrated-circuit design from RTL through logic synthesis, physical design, and signoff, including static timing analysis, design-for-test, and electrical verification.
subdomains.occupations: Digital/RTL design engineer; Physical design (PnR) engineer; DFT engineer; Timing/signoff (STA) engineer
subdomains.boundary_note: Official examples center on RTL-to-GDS EDA flow alignment to a pinned toolchain; new candidates must avoid redoing flow alignment and instead cover synthesis optimization, STA/signoff, and DFT.

subdomains.business_boundary: Analysis and planning of urban transport and land use, including traffic signal/simulation engineering, travel-demand modeling, and GIS-based spatial planning.
subdomains.occupations: Transport modeler/traffic engineer; Travel-demand analyst; Urban/spatial planner; GIS analyst
subdomains.boundary_note: Official examples are SUMO microsimulation calibration and metro passenger simulation; boundary overlaps transport_safety (fire_safety, aviation, maritime) and transit engineering.

subdomains.business_boundary: Design, simulation, and control of robotic manipulation and locomotion systems, including whole-body control, motion planning, grasping, and reinforcement-learning policy learning.
subdomains.occupations: Robotics RL/controls engineer; Manipulation/motion-planning engineer; Whole-body control engineer; Robot software engineer
subdomains.boundary_note: Official examples are humanoid locomotion/whole-body-control policy training and rollout; new candidates must cover manipulation, grasp synthesis, and classical motion planning beyond humanoid-only evaluation.

candidates.workflow_title: Radial distribution network load-flow analysis with distributed energy resource (DER) integration and contingency ranking
candidates.workflow_summary: Build a radial distribution feeder model, run load flow with realistic loads, place renewable DER units, and rank N-1 contingencies by voltage/thermal impact to determine hosting capacity.
candidates.source_reference: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2773153724000975 (radial distribution performance enhancement via renewable integration and comprehensive contingency ranking)
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Feeder single-line diagram, line/transformer impedances, load profiles, candidate DER sites and ratings, voltage/thermal limits.
candidates.usage_permissions: Expert must own or have site-access rights to the network data; synthetic anonymized feeders preferred for a public benchmark.
candidates.task_input: A radial distribution feeder topology with parameters and load/DER data; the task asks for steady-state voltage profile and a contingency ranking.
candidates.professional_operations: Model the feeder, perform backward/forward sweep or Newton-Raphson load flow, place and size DER, simulate each outage scenario, and rank violations.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A load-flow report with bus voltage profiles, DER sizing recommendation, and an ordered N-1 contingency severity table.
candidates.success_criteria: Voltage magnitudes within ANSI/IEC limits, no thermal overloads, and a defensible ranked contingency list matching a reference solution.
candidates.verification_approach: Reproduce results with an independent open-source solver (e.g. pandapower/OpenDSS) and check voltages and contingency order against golden outputs.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux/Windows both viable; Python with pandapower/OpenDSS is open-source; no GPU needed.
candidates.blocking_risks: Proprietary network data may be unavailable; expert must supply a realistic anonymized feeder to avoid a trivial toy problem.
candidates.expert_capability: Power-flow modeling, distribution planning, DER integration, and contingency analysis.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Touches energy_power reliability assessment (wf02) but is a load-flow/DER workflow, not a reliability-index computation.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete end-to-end workflow (model-build to ranked deliverable), not a single operation; distinct method from wf02.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E3 source seen via search snippet only (ScienceDirect paywalled); confirm full method details with the expert.

candidates.workflow_title: Distribution system reliability assessment computing SAIDI/SAIFI/ENS via analytical or Monte Carlo methods
candidates.workflow_summary: Compute standard reliability indices (SAIDI, SAIFI, ENS) for a radial feeder using a sequential analytical/state-transition approach over component failure and repair data.
candidates.source_reference: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0142061525006179 (Continuous-Time Markov Chain sequential analytical reliability assessment for power distribution networks)
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Component failure/repair rates, protection/restoration scheme, load point data, feeder topology.
candidates.usage_permissions: Expert provides anonymized component reliability parameters; benchmark must not depend on a specific utility's confidential outage records.
candidates.task_input: A feeder with component reliability data and load points; the task asks for reliability indices per load point and system-wide.
candidates.professional_operations: Enumerate failure modes, apply analytical or Monte Carlo state-transition evaluation, aggregate interruption durations/frequencies, and compute SAIDI/SAIFI/ENS.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A reliability report with per-load-point and system indices and the dominant failure contributors.
candidates.success_criteria: Computed indices match reference values within tolerance and dominant-contributor ranking is correct.
candidates.verification_approach: Cross-check analytical indices against a Monte Carlo reference and validate with IEEE RBTS-style test feeders.
candidates.blocking_risks: Requires realistic component reliability data; a synthetic standard test feeder (RBTS) is the low-risk fallback.
candidates.expert_capability: Distribution reliability theory, protection/restoration modeling, and reliability-index computation.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps eng_energypower_wf01 on distribution domain but is a distinct reliability-index workflow; flag to avoid double-counting the same feeder task.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete workflow distinct from load-flow/DER (wf01); not a parameter-substitution variant.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E3 source seen via search snippet only; confirm the CTMC method maps to IEEE 1366 index definitions with the expert.

candidates.workflow_title: Whole-building energy model calibration and measurement-and-verification (M&V) to ASHRAE Guideline 14
candidates.workflow_summary: Calibrate a building energy simulation model against metered consumption data and compute normalized energy savings with NMBE/CvRMSE acceptance metrics.
candidates.source_reference: none (project hypothesis); related building-simulation context from https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/1872408 (EnergyPlus step-response training data)
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Metered interval energy data, building geometry/HVAC schedules, weather file, utility bills, and any ECM retrofit records.
candidates.usage_permissions: Metered data must be synthetic or de-identified; expert confirms reuse rights.
candidates.task_input: A building description plus monthly/hourly metered consumption and weather; the task asks for a calibrated model and verified savings.
candidates.professional_operations: Build the baseline model, compare to metered data, tune parameters, compute NMBE/CvRMSE per ASHRAE G14, and estimate normalized savings.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A calibrated model with calibration metrics and an M&V savings report.
candidates.success_criteria: NMBE and CvRMSE within ASHRAE G14 thresholds and savings within an accepted uncertainty band.
candidates.verification_approach: Recompute NMBE/CvRMSE independently from model output and metered series; check thresholds with a script.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux/Windows; EnergyPlus or OpenStudio (open-source); no GPU.
candidates.blocking_risks: Metered data scarcity and model overfitting to calibration targets; must fix a clear acceptance threshold.
candidates.expert_capability: Building energy simulation, calibration methods, and ASHRAE G14 M&V practice.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Adjacent to the official building-MPC example but distinct (calibration/M&V vs control); flag to avoid conflating with mpc_control_building_v1.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete calibration-plus-verification workflow, not a single simulation run.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E4: no direct M&V source this round; MUST be expert-confirmed and grounded in ASHRAE Guideline 14.

candidates.workflow_title: Nuclear reactor fuel-cycle and thermal-hydraulics simulation for a molten salt reactor
candidates.workflow_summary: Simulate nuclide flow and thermal feedback across a molten salt reactor fuel cycle to characterize burnup, breeding, and core thermal behavior.
candidates.source_reference: https://www.nstl.gov.cn/paper_detail.html?doi=10.1002/er.5490 (thermal feedback and nuclide flow effects on molten salt reactor fuel-cycle characteristics)
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Reactor core geometry, salt composition, nuclear data libraries, thermal-hydraulic boundary conditions, and cycle parameters.
candidates.usage_permissions: Public nuclear data libraries (e.g. ENDF) are usable; core design data must be non-sensitive or synthetic.
candidates.task_input: A defined MSR core with salt composition and operating conditions; the task asks for fuel-cycle and thermal characteristics.
candidates.professional_operations: Set up nuclide-transmutation and heat-transport models, couple thermal feedback, run depletion, and report burnup/reactivity/temperature fields.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A fuel-cycle analysis report with nuclide inventories, reactivity/burnup, and thermal behavior.
candidates.success_criteria: Reactivity and temperature results within reference bounds and nuclide inventories match a validated benchmark.
candidates.verification_approach: Compare against published MSR benchmarks or a reduced-order analytic check of mass/energy balance.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux/Windows; Serpent/OpenMC (open-source) plus Python; no GPU required though optional for acceleration.
candidates.blocking_risks: Nuclear data licensing and the specialized skill to build a credible MSR model; a simplified single-cell model is the fallback.
candidates.expert_capability: Reactor physics, thermal-hydraulics, and nuclide-depletion modeling.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Nuclear energy is within energy_power but distinct from power-systems and building candidates; flag no overlap with wf01-wf03.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete coupled physics workflow, not a single depletion step.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E3 source seen via search snippet only (NSTL abstract); confirm modeling scope and benchmark with a nuclear engineer.

candidates.workflow_title: Production decline-curve analysis and estimated ultimate recovery (EUR) forecasting
candidates.workflow_summary: Fit Arps/hyperbolic decline models to well production history, diagnose flow regime, and forecast EUR and remaining reserves.
candidates.source_reference: https://zenodo.org/records/22704685/files/Seeing%20The%20Unseen.pdf?download=1 (hyperbolic decline example qi=980 STB/d, Di=0.42 yr^-1, b=0.65)
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Monthly/daily production rates, flowing pressures, well completion and formation data, and any analog EUR assumptions.
candidates.usage_permissions: Production data must be synthetic or licensed; expert confirms no confidential well identities.
candidates.task_input: A production history series with well metadata; the task asks for decline-model parameters and an EUR forecast.
candidates.professional_operations: Clean the rate data, select decline model, fit parameters, diagnose boundary-dominated vs transient flow, and extrapolate EUR.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A decline-curve fit with parameters, EUR estimate, and forecast with uncertainty bounds.
candidates.success_criteria: Fitted parameters and EUR within tolerance of a reference and correct flow-regime diagnosis.
candidates.verification_approach: Re-fit with an independent library and compare q_i, D_i, b and EUR against golden values on held-out tail data.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux/Windows; Python (numpy/scipy) or R; no GPU.
candidates.blocking_risks: Real production data is confidential; synthetic multi-well datasets must be realistic enough to avoid trivial fits.
candidates.expert_capability: Decline-curve analysis, reserves estimation, and flow-regime recognition.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Related to eng_mining_wf02 (rate-transient analysis) but distinct (empirical decline vs physics-based transient analysis); flag to avoid merging.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete analysis-to-forecast workflow, not a single curve fit.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E3 source seen via search snippet only; confirm Arps/hyperbolic convention (b, D_i) with the expert.

candidates.workflow_title: Rate-transient analysis (RTA) of well bottomhole pressure and flow-rate data for reservoir characterization
candidates.workflow_summary: Use transient bottomhole-pressure and flow-rate data to estimate permeability, skin, and fracture geometry via log-log diagnostic and history matching.
candidates.source_reference: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0920410520306616 (bottomhole pressure and flow-rate transient data analysis)
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Bottomhole pressure vs time, flow rate vs time, fluid PVT properties, and completion geometry.
candidates.usage_permissions: Well data must be synthetic or de-identified; PVT data from public correlations is usable.
candidates.task_input: Time series of bottomhole pressure and flow rate plus PVT; the task asks for reservoir/well parameters.
candidates.professional_operations: Build diagnostic plots (log-log derivative), identify flow regimes, apply analytical RTA models, and match to estimate parameters.
candidates.expected_deliverable: An RTA report with permeability, skin, fracture half-length (if applicable), and uncertainty.
candidates.success_criteria: Estimated parameters within tolerance of a reference and correct flow-regime identification.
candidates.verification_approach: Reproduce the diagnostic derivative and parameter estimates independently and compare to synthetic-truth values.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux/Windows; Python or commercial RTA tools (KAPPA); no GPU.
candidates.blocking_risks: Requires coupled pressure+rate data that real operators rarely release; synthetic data generation is the practical path.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps eng_mining_wf01 (both rate-based reservoir evaluation); ensure distinct objective (characterization vs forecasting).
candidates.granularity_check: Complete diagnostic-to-interpretation workflow, not a single derivative plot.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E3 source seen via search snippet only (ScienceDirect paywalled); confirm which RTA models to scope.

candidates.workflow_title: Ultimate pit limit optimization (Lerchs-Grossmann) and open-pit production scheduling from a block model
candidates.workflow_summary: Compute the optimal ultimate pit shell from a 3D block model using the Lerchs-Grossmann algorithm, then schedule extraction to maximize net present value.
candidates.source_reference: https://revistas.unitru.edu.pe/index.php/jamm/en/article/download/7098/7116/28827 (Lerchs-Grossmann pit-limit optimization in Python); also https://scholar.google.lv/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=xPUlO_0AAAAJ&citation_for_view=xPUlO_0AAAAJ:e5wmG9Sq2KIC (simulated-annealing mine production scheduling)
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Block model (grade/tonnage per block), block economic values, slope angles, and mining/capacity constraints.
candidates.usage_permissions: Expert supplies a synthetic or licensed block model; a public benchmark block model is preferred.
candidates.task_input: A block model with grades and economics plus slope constraints; the task asks for the optimal pit shell and schedule.
candidates.professional_operations: Compute block values, run Lerchs-Grossmann (or max-flow equivalent), then sequence extraction with scheduling constraints to maximize NPV.
candidates.expected_deliverable: An optimal pit shell visualization and a period-by-period extraction schedule with NPV.
candidates.success_criteria: Pit shell matches a reference optimum and the schedule NPV is within tolerance of a reference plan.
candidates.verification_approach: Verify pit optimality against a max-flow formulation and check schedule feasibility and NPV against golden outputs.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux/Windows; Python (optimization libraries) or commercial tools (Whittle/NPV Scheduler); no GPU.
candidates.blocking_risks: Real block models are proprietary; a realistic synthetic block model is needed to avoid trivial solutions.
candidates.expert_capability: Pit optimization, block modeling, and open-pit scheduling economics.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Distinct from eng_mining_wf04 (geomechanics) and wf01/wf02 (petroleum); no overlap.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete optimization-plus-scheduling workflow, not a single pit computation.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E3 sources seen via search snippet only; confirm algorithm variant (LG vs pseudoflow) with the expert.

candidates.workflow_title: Open-pit slope stability analysis using limit-equilibrium factor-of-safety methods
candidates.workflow_summary: Evaluate end-of-pit slope stability by determining structural parameters and computing the factor of safety with limit-equilibrium methods under representative failure modes.
candidates.source_reference: https://opaj.napstic.cn/periodicalArticle/0120240901293708 (structural parameter analysis and stability calculation of end-of-pit slope of a polymetallic mine)
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Rock-mass properties (cohesion, friction, density), joint/persistency data, groundwater conditions, and slope geometry.
candidates.usage_permissions: Expert supplies synthetic or de-identified geotechnical parameters; lab test data must be licensed.
candidates.task_input: A slope cross-section with geotechnical parameters and water conditions; the task asks for the factor of safety and critical slip surface.
candidates.professional_operations: Characterize rock mass, select failure mode, perform limit-equilibrium slices, locate critical slip surface, and compute factor of safety.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A stability report with factor of safety, critical failure surface, and a stability recommendation.
candidates.success_criteria: Factor of safety matches a reference and the critical surface is correctly identified against acceptance criteria.
candidates.verification_approach: Cross-check with an independent limit-equilibrium implementation and compare factor of safety to a golden value.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux/Windows; Python or commercial tools (Slide/Rocscience); no GPU.
candidates.blocking_risks: Geotechnical parameters are site-specific and often confidential; a standardized synthetic slope case is the fallback.
candidates.expert_capability: Rock mechanics, limit-equilibrium slope stability, and geotechnical parameter characterization.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps civil/geotechnical engineering; flag this boundary explicitly for taxonomy placement.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete stability-analysis workflow, not a single slice computation.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E3 source seen via search snippet only; confirm method (Bishop/Morgenstern-Price) with a geomechanics expert.

candidates.workflow_title: Hydraulic fracturing stimulation and well completion design
candidates.workflow_summary: Design a hydraulic fracturing treatment (fluid, proppant, pumping schedule) and completion configuration to stimulate a target reservoir interval.
candidates.source_reference: https://www.rigzone.com/insights/how-it-works-3/how-does-well-fracturing-work-to-stimulate-production-1128/ (how well fracturing works to stimulate production)
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Formation stress profile, permeability/porosity, fracture gradient, fluid/proppant properties, and completion constraints.
candidates.usage_permissions: Expert provides synthetic or de-identified well/formation data; vendor fluid data must be licensed or generalized.
candidates.task_input: A target interval with formation properties; the task asks for a fracturing design and expected stimulated productivity.
candidates.professional_operations: Estimate fracture geometry, select fluid/proppant, size the pumping schedule, and estimate post-frac productivity improvement.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A fracturing design (fluid, proppant, schedule) with predicted fracture geometry and productivity uplift.
candidates.success_criteria: Fracture geometry and productivity uplift within tolerance of a reference and physically consistent with the formation.
candidates.verification_approach: Check design consistency with fracture-geometry models and compare predicted productivity to a reference simulation.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux/Windows; Python or commercial fracture simulators (FracPro/MFrac); no GPU.
candidates.blocking_risks: Proprietary stimulation data and the need for real formation stress data; a synthetic tight-reservoir case is the fallback.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Within mining_petroleum but distinct from reservoir analysis (wf01/wf02); no overlap with mining planning.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete design workflow, not a single fracture-dimension calculation.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E3 source seen via search snippet only (Rigzone 403 on fetch); confirm design scope with a completions expert.

candidates.workflow_title: Static timing analysis (STA) and electrical signoff with EM/IR and physical verification
candidates.workflow_summary: Perform setup/hold timing analysis plus electromigration, IR-drop, and physical (DRC/LVS) checks on a placed-and-routed design to reach signoff closure.
candidates.source_reference: https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3819588 (signoff as final pre-tapeout verification via STA, EM, IR drop, and physical checks)
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Netlist, SDC timing constraints, standard-cell library (liberty/LEF), SPEF parasitics, and PDK signoff rules.
candidates.usage_permissions: Expert must use an open PDK (e.g. SkyWater 130nm) or licensed PDK; library files must be redistributable for a public benchmark.
candidates.task_input: A post-PnR netlist with constraints and parasitics; the task asks for a timing/signoff closure report.
candidates.professional_operations: Run STA to find setup/hold violations, fix timing, run EM/IR and DRC/LVS, and iterate to signoff-clean closure.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A signoff report with timing, EM/IR, and DRC/LVS results and a closed (clean) design.
candidates.success_criteria: Zero remaining setup/hold/EM/IR/DRC/LVS violations against signoff corners, matching a reference closure.
candidates.verification_approach: Reproduce STA and DRC with open-source tools (OpenSTA, Magic/KLayout) and compare violation counts to golden results.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux required (EDA toolchains); OpenSTA/Magic open-source; no GPU.
candidates.blocking_risks: PDK and library licensing; closed-source signoff tools (PrimeTime) may be unavailable, so an open-source equivalence path is needed.
candidates.expert_capability: STA, EM/IR analysis, DRC/LVS, and timing-closure methodology.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Distinct from RTL-to-GDS flow alignment; overlaps physical design but at the signoff stage.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete timing-to-signoff workflow, not a single report generation.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E3 source seen via search snippet only (ACM paywalled); confirm corner set and signoff criteria with the expert.

candidates.workflow_title: Logic synthesis optimization for timing, area, and power closure
candidates.workflow_summary: Synthesize RTL to a gate-level netlist using Design Compiler/Physical Compiler and optimize for timing, area, and power under constraints, then validate with PrimeTime.
candidates.source_reference: https://ebooks.mpdl.mpg.de/ebooks/Record/EB000614072 (Advanced ASIC Chip Synthesis Using Synopsys Design Compiler, Physical Compiler, and PrimeTime)
candidates.expert_raw_materials: RTL source, SDC constraints, target standard-cell library, and optimization goals.
candidates.usage_permissions: RTL must be reusable (open-source or expert-owned); library and tool licenses must permit benchmark redistribution.
candidates.task_input: RTL plus timing constraints and a target library; the task asks for a timing/area/power-optimized gate netlist.
candidates.professional_operations: Elaborate RTL, apply constraints, run synthesis with optimization strategies, and iterate to meet timing/area/power targets.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A synthesized netlist with a QoR report (timing slack, area, power) and constraint checks.
candidates.success_criteria: Netlist meets timing with minimum area/power and matches a reference QoR within tolerance.
candidates.verification_approach: Re-synthesize with Yosys and compare structural/area/timing QoR against golden results.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux required; Yosys open-source; Synopsys tools are proprietary and optional.
candidates.blocking_risks: Proprietary EDA licenses (Design Compiler) may block exact reproduction; an open-source (Yosys) equivalence must be engineered.
candidates.expert_capability: RTL synthesis, timing constraints, and QoR optimization.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Upstream of wf01 signoff and related to, but distinct from, the official RTL-to-GDS flow-alignment tasks.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete RTL-to-netlist optimization workflow, not a single synthesis invocation.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E3 source seen via search snippet only (book record); confirm target library and QoR metrics with the expert.

candidates.workflow_title: Design-for-test (DFT) scan insertion and automatic test-pattern generation (ATPG)
candidates.workflow_summary: Insert scan chains and test logic into a gate-level design and generate ATPG patterns to reach a target stuck-at/transition fault coverage.
candidates.source_reference: none (project hypothesis); DFT is a standard industrial workflow without a directly consulted source this round
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Gate-level netlist, test-mode constraints, scan-chain specifications, and fault models/coverage targets.
candidates.usage_permissions: Expert supplies a synthesizable netlist; test structures and patterns are reusable deliverables.
candidates.task_input: A gate netlist with test requirements; the task asks for a scan-inserted design and fault-coverage report.
candidates.professional_operations: Insert scan chains and test points, run ATPG, compute fault coverage, and iterate to reach coverage targets.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A scan-inserted netlist plus ATPG patterns and a fault-coverage report.
candidates.success_criteria: Target stuck-at/transition fault coverage achieved with minimal area overhead, matching a reference coverage.
candidates.verification_approach: Recompute fault coverage with an open-source ATPG (e.g. TestVector/Atalanta) and compare to golden coverage.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux required; open-source ATPG limited; commercial tools (TetraMAX) may be unavailable.
candidates.blocking_risks: ATPG tooling scarcity in open source; a simplified fault model (stuck-at only) may be needed.
candidates.expert_capability: DFT architecture, scan insertion, and ATPG/coverage analysis.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Distinct from synthesis and signoff; no overlap with official flow-alignment tasks.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete scan-insertion-to-coverage workflow, not a single pattern run.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E4: no direct source; MUST be expert-confirmed and grounded in IEEE 1149.1/scan-ATPG practice.

candidates.workflow_title: Adaptive traffic-signal timing and lane-allocation optimization at an isolated intersection
candidates.workflow_summary: Jointly optimize lane allocation and adaptive signal timing at an isolated intersection under stochastic demand to minimize delay and maximize throughput.
candidates.source_reference: https://trid.trb.org/View/2434453 and https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0968090X24003838 (integrated lane allocation and adaptive signal control under stochastic demand)
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Intersection geometry, turning-movement counts, demand distributions, and signal timing constraints.
candidates.usage_permissions: Expert supplies a representative or synthetic intersection dataset with no personally identifying traffic data.
candidates.task_input: An intersection layout with stochastic demand; the task asks for an optimized lane and signal plan.
candidates.professional_operations: Model arrivals, formulate lane-allocation and signal-timing optimization, solve, and simulate to evaluate delay/queue metrics.
candidates.expected_deliverable: An optimized lane configuration and signal timing plan with delay/throughput evaluation.
candidates.success_criteria: Minimized average delay/queue and throughput within tolerance of a reference optimum.
candidates.verification_approach: Re-simulate the optimized plan in a microsimulator and compare delay/queue metrics to golden values.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux/Windows; Python or SUMO; no GPU.
candidates.blocking_risks: Real demand data may be unavailable; synthetic stochastic demand must be realistic to avoid trivial optima.
candidates.expert_capability: Traffic signal control, intersection capacity, and optimization.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps transport engineering; distinct from SUMO calibration official example (control vs calibration).
candidates.granularity_check: Complete optimization-plus-evaluation workflow, not a single signal calculation.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E3 source seen via search snippet only; confirm objective/metrics with a traffic engineer.

candidates.workflow_title: GIS multi-criteria land-use suitability and zoning overlay analysis
candidates.workflow_summary: Combine weighted spatial criteria layers (e.g. slope, land cover, proximity, utilities) via GIS overlay to produce a land-use suitability and zoning recommendation map.
candidates.source_reference: https://scholar.google.co.th/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=PCZI9gUAAAAJ&sortby=pubdate&citation_for_view=PCZI9gUAAAAJ:9Pw2l-cN0AIC (using GIS and remote sensing for zoning analysis)
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Raster/vector base layers (DEM, land cover, roads, utilities), criterion weights, and zoning constraints.
candidates.usage_permissions: Public geodata (e.g. OpenStreetMap, public DEM) is usable; proprietary parcel data requires permission.
candidates.task_input: A study area with spatial layers and criteria; the task asks for a suitability and zoning map.
candidates.professional_operations: Standardize layers, apply weights, perform weighted overlay, and classify the result into suitability/zoning classes.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A suitability map with classification and a zoning recommendation with justification.
candidates.success_criteria: Suitability classes match a reference overlay and criterion weights are applied correctly.
candidates.verification_approach: Reproduce the overlay in geopandas/QGIS and compare classified output to golden rasters.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux/Windows; QGIS or Python (geopandas/rasterio); no GPU.
candidates.blocking_risks: Weighting subjectivity makes scoring fuzzy; must pin an objective scoring rule or golden reference.
